budgetRationale: Re-baselined for the commit graph that an outside host can embed: +23.0 KiB on the entrypoint against the quick-fixes pin, of which +18.8 KiB is graph.js, +2.7 KiB graph.css and +1.5 KiB shared.js, putting the entrypoint 11.0 KiB over its ceiling. About 20 KiB of it is this change, measured on the previous core: the host surface (header, message and ref metadata options, a host's own localizer, a keymap registrar per graph, embed and drive methods, the typed event map), the full-color token defaults, and the metadata requests and redraws limited to rows on screen; the rest had accrued on core since caaf7ef. Ceilings keep their prior allowances above the new baseline. Before that: Re-pinned for three Commit Graph quick fixes (#5352, #5607, #2925): the entrypoint grows +9.2 KiB against the Review Changes pin, but only about 0.6 KiB of it is this change (graph.js +0.25 KiB, graph.css +0.39 KiB): main measured 3,257,438 bytes at caaf7ef (and the same at 1e435c5), inside its ceiling, so +8.5 KiB (mostly graph.js) had already accrued there since 2e2557e. This change's bytes are Compare Working Tree to Here using a commit, stash or tag row's own ref; the Changes column opt-in overlay's shrinkable spacers and size container queries that drop its help copy and Hide link whole on a short rows area; and the hidden branches/tags popover's capped, scrollable list with the shared scrollbar styles. Not a new dependency or a module moving between chunks. Ceilings keep their prior headroom: 12 KiB above baseline on the entrypoint, 4 KiB on shared.js (loaded by every webview), and graph.css's accounted allowance.
